name: What prep work matters most before pool resurfacing?

mainEntity.name: Which preparation steps most affect how long a new pool surface will last?
mainEntity.text: Which preparation steps most affect how long a new pool surface will last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prep is one of the biggest factors in resurfacing success. The old finish has to be drained, cleaned, and checked for weak areas, then all loose or damaged material should be removed before the new surface goes on. Cracks, voids, and any bond failures need repair so the new finish is not sitting on a moving or unstable base. Proper prep also includes protecting fittings, establishing a bonding surface, and confirming that the shell is ready for the chosen material. In the Los Angeles area, where pools may be older and have been repaired multiple times, prep quality is often more important than the brand name of the finish. Homeowners should ask exactly how the contractor handles chip-out, patching, and bonding. A cheap quote that skimps on prep can lead to peeling, roughness, or early resurfacing failure.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most important prep work includes draining, removing weak material, repairing cracks, cleaning the shell, and creating a strong bond for the new finish. Skipping prep can lead to peeling, hollow spots, or early failure. Surface prep matters as much as the finish itself because the new layer can only last if it bonds well to the base.
